literal: Whatever the funeral rites require shall be supplied from public funds as needed.
idiomatic: Whatever the funeral required was to be supplied from public funds.

literal: " Yuan Kang's mother the Lady Li, after Yuan Kang's death, grieved until illness took her and she died; posthumously granted Lady of Guangzong commandery, posthumous title Zhenzhao.
idiomatic: " Yuan Kang's mother, Lady Li, after his death grieved herself into illness and died; she was posthumously granted Lady of Guangzong commandery with the posthumous title Zhenzhao.

literal: Yuan Kang's son Shancang was mild and elegant, with discerning judgment; at the end of Wuping he held acting insignia equal to three masters of ceremonies and was attendant of the yellow gate.
idiomatic: Yuan Kang's son Shancang was mild and elegant, with a keen eye for men; at the end of Wuping he held acting insignia equal to three masters of ceremonies and served as attendant of the yellow gate.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
idiomatic: Under Sui, in the Kaihuang era, he was vice director of the ministry of rites.

literal: Early in Daye he died as superintendent of Pengcheng commandery.
idiomatic: Early in Daye he died while serving as superintendent of Pengcheng commandery.

literal: Yuan Kang's younger brother Chen reached office as grand messenger.
idiomatic: Yuan Kang's younger brother Chen rose to grand messenger.

literal: Next, Ji Zhuan was grand administrator of Julu, then transferred to aide-de-camp of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Next came Ji Zhuan, grand administrator of Julu, then aide-de-camp of Ji Province.

literal: When the Prince of Ping'an Wang Guiyan rebelled, Ji Zhuan held to his integrity and would not follow, and was killed for it.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Ping'an Wang Guiyan rebelled, Ji Zhuan held to his integrity and refused to join him, and was killed for it.

literal: Posthumously granted commandant of the guards and governor of Zhao Province.
idiomatic: He was posthumously granted commandant of the guards and governor of Zhao Province.

literal: Du Bi, styled Fuxuan, was a native of Quyang in Zhongshan; his childhood name was Fuguo.
idiomatic: Du Bi, styled Fuxuan, came from Quyang in Zhongshan; his childhood name was Fuguo.

literal: In his own preface he said he was originally from Dulang in Jingzhao; his ninth-generation ancestor Ao was Jin attendant cavalry regular and, on a mission, was lost in Zhao and settled there.
idiomatic: In his own preface he said he was originally from Dulang in Jingzhao; his ninth-generation ancestor Ao had been Jin attendant cavalry regular and, on a mission, was stranded in Zhao and settled there.

literal: His grandfather Yanheng was grand administrator of Huainan.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yanheng had been grand administrator of Huainan.

literal: His father Cidu was magistrate of Fanzhi.
idiomatic: His father Cidu had been magistrate of Fanzhi.

literal: From youth Bi was clever; the family was poor and had no books; at twelve he lodged at the district school to study, and at the sacrificial rites of instruction the teachers always marveled at him.
idiomatic: From youth Bi was clever; the family was poor and owned no books; at twelve he lodged at the district school. At the sacrificial rites of instruction his teachers always marveled at him.

literal: Fellow-district man Zhen Chen was long secretary of Ding Province; he selected and tested the students, saw Bi, and questioned him; his explanations were clear and refined and his answers came like echoes; Chen greatly admired him.
idiomatic: His fellow townsman Zhen Chen was long secretary of Ding Province; he selected and tested students, saw Bi, and questioned him. Bi's explanations were clear and his answers came like echoes; Chen was greatly struck by him.

literal: Chen's son Kuan became Bi's friend.
idiomatic: Chen's son Kuan became Bi's friend.

literal: Provincial governor Prince of Rencheng Cheng heard of him and summoned him for questioning; he deeply praised him and promised him talent fit for a king's aide.
idiomatic: Provincial governor Prince of Rencheng Cheng heard of him and summoned him for questioning, praised him deeply, and declared him fit to serve a king's right hand.

literal: Cheng and Chen returned to Luoyang and praised him at court; the chancellor Prince of Gaoyang and others repeatedly invited him.
idiomatic: Cheng and Chen returned to Luoyang and praised him at court; the chancellor Prince of Gaoyang and others repeatedly sought him out.

literal: In the Yan Chang era he began his career through military merit and was made general of Guangwu and clerk in the ink office of Hengzhou's expeditionary command, managing records.
idiomatic: In the Yan Chang era he entered service through military merit as general of Guangwu and clerk in the ink office of Hengzhou's expeditionary command, where he managed records.

literal: Bi excelled at documents and was always recommended by his contemporaries.
idiomatic: Bi excelled at documents and was always recommended by his contemporaries.

literal: Early in Xiao Chang he was made erudite of the Imperial Academy, concurrently acting legal clerk in the Prince of Guangyang's rapid-cavalry office, and chief of the traveling staff's income-and-expenditure section.
idiomatic: Early in Xiao Chang he was made erudite of the Imperial Academy, concurrently acting legal clerk in the Prince of Guangyang's rapid-cavalry office, and chief of the traveling staff's income-and-expenditure section.

literal: On returning he was made magistrate of Qucheng in Guang Province.
idiomatic: On returning he was made magistrate of Qucheng in Guang Province.

literal: His government was quiet and clean; he strove for full humanity and clemency; lawsuits ceased, and he was praised near and far.
idiomatic: His government was quiet and clean; he strove for humanity and clemency; lawsuits ceased, and he was praised near and far.

literal: The age was full of troubles and bandits were everywhere; when military service was conscripted many fled and rebelled on the roads, and the court worried over it.
idiomatic: The age was full of troubles and bandits were everywhere; when troops were conscripted many fled or rebelled on the roads, and the court was troubled.

literal: Therefore soldiers were ordered to carry their military gear, with separate carts transporting it along the road;
idiomatic: Soldiers were therefore ordered to carry their own gear, with separate carts transporting it along the road;

literal: magistrates were also ordered to escort their men personally to the army camp.
idiomatic: magistrates were also ordered to escort their men personally to the army camp.

literal: When Guang Province sent troops, Bi escorted his district as far as Beihai commandery; the provincial soldiers scattered at once, but only those Bi escorted did not stir.
idiomatic: When Guang Province sent troops, Bi escorted his district as far as Beihai commandery; the provincial soldiers scattered at once, but only the men Bi escorted held firm.

literal: Rebel soldiers from other districts all came to attack and rob them, wishing to go away together.
idiomatic: Rebel soldiers from other districts came to attack and rob them, urging them to flee together.

literal: Bi led his personal troops to fight; in the end none would follow the rebels, and they all reached the army camp together.
idiomatic: Bi led his personal troops to fight; in the end none would join the rebels, and they all reached the army camp together.

literal: Army clerk Cui Zhong reported the matter upward.
idiomatic: Army clerk Cui Zhong reported the matter upward.

literal: Such was his winning of men's hearts.
idiomatic: Such was his hold on men's hearts.

literal: In Pu Tai the personnel bureau sent inquiry for outstanding magistrates; Bi had already been replaced and returned, and Donglai grand administrator Wang Xin nominated Bi in response.
idiomatic: In Pu Tai the personnel bureau sought outstanding magistrates; Bi had already left office and returned home, and Donglai grand administrator Wang Xin nominated him in response.

literal: Bi's father was in the district and was killed by bandits; Bi observed mourning for six years.
idiomatic: Bi's father was in the district and was killed by bandits; Bi observed mourning for six years.

literal: Through regular assignment he was made censor, with the added titles forward general and grand master for splendid happiness, and headed the bureau's internal rectifier of characters.
idiomatic: Through regular assignment he was made censor, with the added titles forward general and grand master for splendid happiness, and headed the bureau's internal rectifier of characters.

literal: All impeachments in the bureau were Bi's work.
idiomatic: All impeachments in the bureau were Bi's work.

literal: Memorial documents submitted by censors on missions were entrusted to Bi for review before implementation.
idiomatic: Memorial documents submitted by censors on missions were entrusted to Bi for review before they were implemented.

literal: He was promoted to general of the central army and staff major in the Northern Yu Province rapid-cavalry grand general's office.
idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the central army and staff major in the Northern Yu Province rapid-cavalry grand general's office.

literal: Before he took office, equal in insignia Dou Tai commanded troops on the western campaign, and an edict made Bi Dou's supervising army officer.
idiomatic: Before he took office, Dou Tai, equal in insignia, commanded the western campaign, and an edict made Bi his supervising army officer.

literal: When Tai was defeated and killed himself, Bi fled back with six of his men; Governor of Shan Province Liu Gui shackled and sent them to Jinyang.
idiomatic: When Tai was defeated and killed himself, Bi fled back with six of his men; the governor of Shan Province, Liu Gui, shackled and sent them to Jinyang.

literal: Gao Huan interrogated him, saying: "Commandant Dou on this expedition — I had beforehand set out the proper use, yet he disobeyed my words and brought defeat on himself.
idiomatic: Gao Huan interrogated him, saying, "Commandant Dou on this expedition — I had already laid down how he was to act, yet he disobeyed my words and brought defeat on himself.

literal: Why did you not speak a single word in remonstrance?
idiomatic: Why did you not speak a single word in remonstrance?"

literal: " Bi replied: "A petty clerk with brush and knife, with only slight skill in letters — on matters of convenience debate was not within my reach.
idiomatic: Bi replied, "A petty clerk with brush and knife, with only slight skill in letters — on matters of convenience debate was not within my reach."

literal: " Gao Huan grew angrier.
idiomatic: Gao Huan grew angrier.

literal: Thanks to Fang Mo's remonstrance he was spared.
idiomatic: Thanks to Fang Mo's remonstrance he was spared.

literal: He was demoted to staff major at Xia Guan garrison.
idiomatic: He was demoted to staff major at Xia Guan garrison.

literal: Early in Yuanxiang Gao Huan summoned Bi as acting legal clerk in the great chancellor's office, assigned him to secretariat duties, transferred him to chief of the great traveling staff, and soon added general who pacifies the south.
idiomatic: Early in Yuanxiang Gao Huan summoned Bi as acting legal clerk in the great chancellor's office, assigned him to secretariat duties, made him chief of the great traveling staff, and soon added general who pacifies the south.

literal: Gao Huan also brought Bi in to manage secrets and greatly trusted him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan also brought Bi in to manage secrets and greatly trusted him.

literal: Sometimes when hurried there was no time for a written instruction; he would hand blank paper and order Bi to read aloud at once.
idiomatic: Sometimes when hurried there was no time for a written instruction; he would hand Bi blank paper and order him to read aloud at once.

literal: Bi once seized an opportunity privately to urge Gao Huan to accept the Wei abdication; Gao Huan raised his staff and drove him off.
idiomatic: Bi once seized a private moment to urge Gao Huan to accept the Wei abdication; Gao Huan raised his staff and drove him off.

literal: Chancellery legal clerk Xin Ziyan, on consultation matters, said they must take the signature; Ziyan read "signature" as "tree."
idiomatic: Chancellery legal clerk Xin Ziyan, on a consultation matter, said they must take the signature; Ziyan read shu (signature) as shu (tree).

literal: Gao Huan raged: "The little man does not even know to avoid another's taboo name!
idiomatic: Gao Huan raged, "The little man does not even know to avoid another's taboo name!"

literal: " He had him beaten before the assembly.
idiomatic: He had him beaten before the assembly.

literal: Bi advanced: "In the Rites, when there are two names one does not avoid half of either; Confucius speaking of Zheng would not say Zai, and speaking of Zai would not say Zheng.
idiomatic: Bi advanced, "In the Rites, when there are two names one does not avoid half of either; Confucius speaking of Zheng would not say Zai, and speaking of Zai would not say Zheng.

literal: Ziyan's crime, by reason, might be forgiven.
idiomatic: Ziyan's crime, by reason, might be forgiven."

literal: " Gao Huan cursed him: "Seeing a man angry, you still drag in the classics and cite the Rites!
idiomatic: Gao Huan cursed him, "Seeing a man angry, you still drag in the classics and cite the Rites!"

literal: " He ordered him out with a shout.
idiomatic: He ordered him out with a shout.

literal: Bi had gone about ten paces when he was called back; Ziyan also received release and forgiveness.
idiomatic: Bi had gone about ten paces when he was called back; Ziyan also received release and forgiveness.

literal: The heir apparent in the capital heard of it and said to Yang Yin: "At the king's side we rely on this man's uprightness; perhaps all under heaven will benefit, not our house alone."
idiomatic: The heir apparent in the capital heard of it and said to Yang Yin, "At the king's side we rely on this man's uprightness; perhaps all under heaven will benefit, not our house alone."

literal: Because civil and military officials in office rarely had integrity, Bi spoke of it to Gao Huan.
idiomatic: Because civil and military officials in office rarely had integrity, Bi spoke of it to Gao Huan.

literal: Gao Huan said: "Bi, come — I will speak to you.
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Bi, come — I will speak to you.

literal: All under heaven is turbid and chaotic; the custom is long-standing.
idiomatic: All under heaven is turbid and chaotic; the custom is long-standing.

literal: Now the supervisors' and generals' families are mostly in Guanxi; Hei La often invites and entices them, and men's hearts whether to stay or go are unsettled.
idiomatic: Now the supervisors' and generals' families are mostly in Guanxi; Hei La often invites and entices them, and men's hearts whether to stay or go are unsettled.

literal: In Jiangdong there is again an old Wu fellow, Xiao Yan, who devotes himself to caps and robes, rites and music; Central Plain scholars look to him as where the true calendar lies.
idiomatic: In Jiangdong there is again an old Wu fellow, Xiao Yan, who devotes himself to caps and robes, rites and music; Central Plain scholars look to him as where the true calendar lies.

literal: If I hastily make a net of law and do not spare them, I fear the supervisors and generals will all go to Hei La and the scholars all flee to Xiao Yan — then people scatter; how can there be a state?
idiomatic: If I hastily make a net of law and show no forbearance, I fear the supervisors and generals will all go to Hei La and the scholars all flee to Xiao Yan — then people scatter; how can there be a state?

literal: You should wait a little; I do not forget this.
idiomatic: You should wait a little; I do not forget this."

literal: When the Sha Yuan campaign was about to come, Bi again asked to first remove the inner traitors, then strike the outer enemies.
idiomatic: When the Sha Yuan campaign was about to begin, Bi again asked to remove the inner traitors first, then strike the outer enemies.

literal: Gao Huan asked who the inner traitors were.
idiomatic: Gao Huan asked who the inner traitors were.

literal: Bi said: "All the meritorious nobles who plunder the myriad people."
idiomatic: Bi said, "All the meritorious nobles who plunder the myriad people."

literal: Gao Huan did not answer; he then ordered the soldiers all to draw bows with arrows nocked, raise knives, and press spears along the road, made Bi pass through among them, and said: "Surely there will be no harm."
idiomatic: Gao Huan did not answer; he then ordered soldiers to draw bows with arrows nocked, raise knives, and press spears along the road, made Bi pass through among them, and said, "Surely there will be no harm."

literal: Bi trembled in fear, sweat streaming.
idiomatic: Bi trembled in fear, sweat streaming.

literal: Gao Huan then explained: "Though arrows are aimed they will not shoot; though knives are raised they will not strike; though spears are pressed they will not stab — yet you still lose soul and gall utterly.
idiomatic: Gao Huan then explained, "Though arrows are aimed they will not shoot; though knives are raised they will not strike; though spears are pressed they will not stab — yet you still lose soul and gall utterly.

literal: The meritorious men touch sharp edges bodily — a hundred deaths, one life; even if their greed is base, what they take is great; they cannot be treated by the usual rule."
idiomatic: The meritorious men touch sharp edges with their bodies — a hundred deaths, one life; even if their greed is base, what they take is great; they cannot be treated by the usual rule."

literal: Bi was then greatly afraid; bowing his forehead he thanked him: "Foolish and without wisdom, not knowing the ultimate principle; now receiving enlightenment I first see the sage and penetrating mind."
idiomatic: Bi was then greatly afraid; bowing his forehead he thanked him, "Foolish and without wisdom, not knowing the ultimate principle; now, enlightened, I first see the sage and penetrating mind."

literal: Later, following Gao Huan, he defeated Western Wei at Mount Mang; ordered to compose the victory bulletin, Bi wrote on silk at once by hand without ever drafting first.
idiomatic: Later, following Gao Huan, he defeated Western Wei at Mount Mang; ordered to compose the victory bulletin, Bi wrote on silk at once by hand without ever drafting first.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Dingyang county with a fief of two hundred households and was added direct attendant cavalry regular and central army general.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Dingyang county with a fief of two hundred households and was added direct attendant cavalry regular and central army general.

literal: On mission to the court the Wei emperor saw him in the Hall of Nine Dragons and said: "When I first read the Zhuangzi I encountered the name of Qin; surely you embody the Way and attain the true, mystery same and all things equal.
idiomatic: On mission to the court the Wei emperor received him in the Hall of Nine Dragons and said, "When I first read the Zhuangzi I encountered the name of Qin; surely you embody the Way and attain the true, mystery same and all things equal.

literal: Hearing you are skilled in learning, I have a question.
idiomatic: Hearing you are skilled in learning, I have a question.

literal: In the sutras, are Buddha-nature and dharma-nature one or different?
idiomatic: In the sutras, are Buddha-nature and dharma-nature one or different?"

literal: " Bi replied: "Buddha-nature and dharma-nature are only one principle."
idiomatic: Bi replied, "Buddha-nature and dharma-nature are only one principle."

literal: The edict again asked: "If Buddha-nature is already not dharma-nature, how can they be one?"
idiomatic: The emperor again asked, "If Buddha-nature is already not dharma-nature, how can they be one?"

literal: He replied: "Nature is nowhere not present; therefore one does not speak of two."
idiomatic: He replied, "Nature is nowhere not present; therefore one does not speak of two."

literal: The edict again asked: "Speakers all say dharma-nature is broad and Buddha-nature narrow; broad and narrow already distinct — if not two, how?"
idiomatic: The emperor again asked, "Speakers all say dharma-nature is broad and Buddha-nature narrow; broad and narrow are already distinct — if not two, how?"

literal: Bi again replied: "In the broad it becomes broad, in the narrow it becomes narrow; if one discusses the substance of nature, it is neither broad nor narrow."
idiomatic: Bi again replied, "In the broad it becomes broad, in the narrow it becomes narrow; if one discusses the substance of nature, it is neither broad nor narrow."

literal: The edict asked: "Since you say it becomes broad and becomes narrow, how can it be neither broad nor narrow?
idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Since you say it becomes broad and becomes narrow, how can it be neither broad nor narrow?

literal: If fixed as narrow, it also cannot become broad."
idiomatic: If fixed as narrow, it also cannot become broad."

literal: He replied: "Because it is not broad or narrow, therefore it can become broad or narrow; what broad and narrow become may differ, but what can become is constantly one."
idiomatic: He replied, "Because it is not broad or narrow, therefore it can become broad or narrow; what broad and narrow become may differ, but what can become is constantly one."

literal: The emperor was pleased and praised it as good.
idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and praised it as good.

literal: He then led him into the sutra library and granted one copy of the Dizhi Sutra and one hundred bolts of silk.
idiomatic: He then led him into the sutra library and granted one copy of the Dizhi Sutra and one hundred bolts of silk.

literal: Prince of Pingyang Yan was governor of Bing Province; Gao Huan also ordered Bi concurrently as chief clerk of Bing's rapid-cavalry office.
idiomatic: Prince of Pingyang Yan was governor of Bing Province; Gao Huan also ordered Bi to serve concurrently as chief clerk of Bing's rapid-cavalry office.

literal: By nature Bi loved subtle principle and tasted the profundities of the Way; from his time in the army he carried sutras on campaign.
idiomatic: By nature Bi loved subtle principle and tasted the profundities of the Way; from his time in the army he carried sutras on campaign.

literal: He annotated Laozi's Daode Jing in two juan and memorialized: "Your servant has heard that riding the wind one adjusts the arrow and pursues swift feathers in high clouds;
idiomatic: He annotated Laozi's Daode Jing in two juan and memorialized, "Your servant has heard that riding the wind one adjusts the arrow and pursues swift feathers in high clouds;

literal: standing by the wave one commands the hook and draws submerged scales from the great abyss.
idiomatic: standing by the wave one commands the hook and draws submerged scales from the great abyss.

literal: If one obtains its Way one masters the work; in things it is so, in principle likewise naturally so.
idiomatic: If one obtains its Way one masters the work; in things it is so, in principle likewise naturally so.

literal: I venture to consider the two classics Dao and De — they illuminate the dark utmost; their purport is dark in motion and stillness; their use pervades common and sage.
idiomatic: I venture to consider the two classics Dao and De — they illuminate the dark utmost; their purport is dark in motion and stillness; their use pervades common and sage.

literal: Speaking of practice: pure, quiet, soft and yielding; speaking of traces: success and achieving order.
idiomatic: Speaking of practice: pure, quiet, soft and yielding; speaking of traces: success and achieving order.

literal: Truly the Yangtze and sea among all streams, the root of all arts.
idiomatic: Truly the Yangtze and sea among all streams, the root of all arts.

literal: Your servant from youth browsed sutras and was especially devoted; though serving in the army office he did not abandon leisure pursuit.
idiomatic: Your servant from youth browsed sutras and was especially devoted; though serving in the army office he did not abandon leisure pursuit.

literal: Drilling into the flavor long, patterns emerged as if he had insight; compared with earlier commentaries he slightly judged them different from the old doctrine.
idiomatic: Drilling into the flavor long, patterns emerged as if he had insight; compared with earlier commentaries he slightly judged them different from the old doctrine.

literal: Feeling arising within and manifesting without, lightly using a tube to peer, thus became forced interpretation.
idiomatic: Feeling arising within and manifesting without, lightly using a tube to peer, he thus produced forced interpretation.

literal: No borrowing from the roaming blade; shame before the wielding axe.
idiomatic: No borrowing from the roaming blade; shame before the wielding axe."
